admission.justification: Selected stored tests check content-before-number pairing, same-number fallback and a singleton between paired neighbours. The monotone and crossed fully-paired controls each check exact pairing for one 2000-reference fixture and elapsed < 10 seconds. Those are bounded single-size regressions, not a multi-size near-linear scaling measurement or a guarantee that every rescanning implementation would fail; the near-linear implementation claim rests on the live-unpaired/Fenwick source analysis.

applicability: Every both-changed card: base with incoming and base with own, plus partnerless own with partnerless incoming.
conditions: Each reference pairs at most once; tests a, b, c apply in that order.
Fully paired inputs do bounded near-linear work through the live unpaired index.
exclusions: References occurring more than once on a side, for which unique-content test a does not apply; the same references remain eligible for same-number test b and singleton-gap test c.

evidence: Rationale: _pair_with_base implements tests a/b/c in order with at-most-once pairing; each gap interval now counts and locates its live numbers in a Fenwick index over number order (O(log n) range count/locate/remove) instead of filtering full side slices, so overlapping crossed intervals never rescan paired populations; base ranges stay disjoint. partnered_incoming holds only incoming numbers whose base also has an own partner. Observed: the exact sealed witness returns {1:1,4:4,7:2,10:6,2:3,8:5} (test_gap_pairing_accounts_live_unpaired_numbers_per_interval); test_partnerless_incoming_pairs_directly_with_partnerless_own (B4->B1, X->6, one B, no B conflict); test_rule_2b_pairs_same_numbers_when_content_cannot (mutant-probed b-alone discriminator); test_gap_pairing_scales_near_linearly_on_fully_paired_inputs plus test_gap_pairing_scales_on_crossed_fully_paired_inputs (2000 refs, monotone and crossed, both green with wide margins).

statement: Rule 2 pairing: base with incoming and base with own by unique content, then same number, then singleton gap; partnerless own/incoming pair by content only; empty-base cards pair against an empty population
